question: Should experimental Claws be allowed to register and share global executable MCP declarations, and if so what host authorization and command-brokering contract is required?
rationale: This is a product and trust-boundary choice: a mechanical patch cannot safely decide whether global MCP entries are agent-scoped, host-shared, brokered, or prohibited.

options.title: Define and enforce a brokered global contract
options.body: Approve the feature direction only after the RFC defines host-authorized sharing and the PR restricts stdio commands to a brokered or explicit allowlisted path.

options.title: Scope MCP ownership per Claw
options.body: Make declarations agent/install scoped so one Claw cannot create or reuse a global capability without a deliberate host-level sharing action.

options.title: Pause the MCP lifecycle slice
options.body: Keep this stacked draft out of core until maintainers decide whether the capability belongs in the Claw lifecycle at all.

recommendation.title: Define and enforce a brokered global contract
recommendation.body: Approve the feature direction only after the RFC defines host-authorized sharing and the PR restricts stdio commands to a brokered or explicit allowlisted path.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick is assigned to this PR and has already reviewed the lifecycle and persistence contracts that the decision governs.
